s: A company has a platform that consists of an on-premises single-node Kubernetes cluster. The cluster uses Windows-based and Linux-based file storage as shared storage. The company wants to migrate its platform to AWS. The cluster has multiple containerized applications that are continuously scanned for operating system vulnerabilities and programming language package vulnerabilities. The company needs a highly available solution that supports monitoring, logging, and multiprotocol shared storage. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
o: Replace the existing Kubernetes cluster with a single-node Amazon EKS cluster that is managed by AWS. Install Prometheus and Grafana on the EKS cluster by using public Docker images. Store the application Docker images in Amazon ECR. Enable ECR enhanced scanning.

Replace the existing Kubernetes cluster with a multi-node Amazon EKS cluster that is managed by AWS. Set up Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon Managed Grafana for monitoring. Store the application Docker images in Amazon ECR. Enable ECR enhanced scanning.

Replace the existing Kubernetes cluster with a multi-node Amazon EKS cluster that is managed by AWS. Install open source versions of Prometheus and Grafana on Amazon EC2 instances. Store the application Docker images in Amazon ECR. Enable ECR enhanced scanning.

Provision an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file share and an Amazon EFS file system. Mount the file share and the file system on the containers launched on the Amazon EKS cluster as persistent volumes.
Provision an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Mount the file system on the containers launched on the Amazon EKS cluster as a persistent volume.
e: B and E are correct. A multi-node Amazon EKS cluster provides high availability for the Kubernetes control and workload layer, while Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon Managed Grafana reduce monitoring overhead compared with self-managed Prometheus and Grafana. Amazon ECR enhanced scanning is also appropriate because it uses Amazon Inspector to scan container images for operating system and programming language package vulnerabilities. For storage, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the correct multiprotocol shared file system because it supports access patterns such as NFS and SMB through a fully managed service. EFS plus FSx for Windows splits storage across two services and does not provide one multiprotocol storage platform. A single-node EKS cluster is not highly available.

w.y: 'Highly available', 'monitoring and logging' and 'multiprotocol shared storage' with 'LEAST operational overhead' point to managed services. A multi-node EKS cluster with Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, Amazon Managed Grafana and ECR enhanced scanning covers the compute side, and FSx for NetApp ONTAP serves NFS and SMB from one file system.

o.A: A single-node cluster is not highly available, and self-installed Prometheus and Grafana add work.
o.B: Correct: multi-node EKS, managed Prometheus and Grafana, ECR enhanced scanning for OS and language packages.
o.C: Running Prometheus and Grafana on your own EC2 instances adds operational work.
o.D: Two separate file systems is more to manage than one multiprotocol file system.
o.E: Correct: FSx for NetApp ONTAP gives shared NFS and SMB access from one file system.
